A_open.text: Saturday. Market day. Town Square is a maze of stalls: honey, raven hats, and fake pumpkins.
The McVine stand holds a pile of pumpkins and a hand-painted sign: McVINE PUMPKINS. HAND-TALKED.
Uncle Gord, I'm not a salesman. I'm a student with a flag.
Smile. Say the price. Don't blink.
McVine! Bringing the new kid? He looks like he'd haggle with a sneeze.
My pumpkins are small and sane. Yours hum.
Three customers today. Charm, guilt, or bluff. Pick right.
Walk up to each customer and press Action. Choose to haggle with charm, guilt, or a bluff.

haggle_hollis.text: Mrs. Hollis, a tiny retiree with a knitting bag, eyes a big pumpkin. She likes polite young men.
Dear, thirty dollars? I only have twenty.

haggle_hollis.prompt: How do you haggle with Mrs. Hollis?

do.text: For you, Mrs. Hollis? Twenty is perfect. This one asked for you by name.
Oh, aren't you sweet! Here's twenty-five!
Think of the pumpkin's feelings.
Young man, I've buried three husbands. Don't guilt me. Fifteen.
It's a rare heirloom!
I knew Gord's grandmother. It's a pumpkin. Fifteen.

haggle_dean.text: A pompous man in a bow tie examines a pumpkin through a monocle. His name tag reads: DEAN WHITLOCK.
I require a pumpkin of distinction. Something that says: authority.
A squirrel pops up on the next stall. The Dean freezes. He does not breathe.
Do not look at it. Do not make eye contact. It is looking at me.

haggle_dean.prompt: How do you haggle with Dean Whitlock?

do.text: You look like a man of taste, Dean.
I do not require your affection, young man. Ten dollars.
A farm family is counting on you.
I feel nothing. Ten dollars.
An heirloom Ravenwood variety. Only three exist. The other two are in the Smithsonian.
Three! I'll take it! Do you have a certificate? Fifty dollars!

haggle_dean.text: The Dean walks off with his pumpkin, glancing over his shoulder at the squirrel the entire way.

haggle_tobias.text: A young father with twin toddlers in a wagon eyes the pumpkins. The twins stare at the biggest.
We're just looking. I'll give you... fifteen. For the small one.

haggle_tobias.prompt: How do you haggle with Tobias?

do.text: Great kids. They'll go far.
I'm exhausted. Fifteen.
The twins would love the big one. It would be a shame if they went home with a small, sad pumpkin.
...Ugh. Fine. FINE. Full price.
A rare heirloom.
I have a master's in horticulture. Fifteen.

then.text: Not bad, boy. Not bad at all.
Dang. That kid's got a gift.

else.text: Thin. We'll make it up. Somehow.

B_gourd.text: A tall figure approaches. Trench coat buttoned to the chin. Saucer sunglasses. A glued-on mustache.
Good day. I would like forty pumpkins. For carving. Which I enjoy. As a man.
Forty?
Yes. The large variety. From the back field. Patch... what number? Seven.
Gord stands very still. He studies the stranger for a long moment. Then he nods.
Full price.
Done.
FULL price? Nobody pays full price! He didn't even haggle!
Sir, your name? For the receipt.
Mr. Gourd. G-O-U-R-D. Like the vegetable.
It's a fruit.
...Like the fruit.
He pays in cash, exact change. And tips in pumpkin seeds.
Exact change. Pumpkin seeds. That's the man from Georgia's cafe.
A white van pulls up. A faculty parking permit hangs in the windshield.
Gord loads forty glowing pumpkins himself.
Gord shakes Mr. Gourd's hand. For a very long time.
Uncle Gord. Do you know that man?
Regular.
He's never been here.
Regular in spirit.
Brad! Twelve pumpkins, please! Back patch! For the Halloween dance punch!

then.text: And I'm mixing them one to four with regular pumpkins, like you said. Thank you again!

else.text: Georgia. Two hundred cups. A full moon. A dance. Those pumpkins hold the thirty minutes.

else.prompt: Georgia is already counting out the money.

options.text: Warn her not to use them

do.text: Georgia. Dilute them. Mix in regular pumpkins. Please. Two hundred people at once is a lot of honesty.
...Oh. I hadn't thought about the crowd.
One to four. I'll dilute. Thank you for telling me.
...Never mind. It'll be great.
It'll be the best punch Ravenwood has ever tasted!
She hugs a twelve-pumpkin wheelbarrow and rolls away, humming. The pumpkins hum back.

B_gourd.text: The van starts. It pulls away from the curb, heading for the college.
Uncle Gord, I need ten minutes.
Take twenty.
Follow the van. Walk toward the college gate and press Action at anything in the way.

do.text: A vendor's cart of knitted raven hats tips over. Brad dives, rolls, and comes up wearing three of them.
I'll pay for those!
Students block the street. Brad squeezes through, apologizing to nine people and a goat.
The van's getting away!

B_dock.text: The loading dock behind the science building. The van's back doors are open. Crates line the dock.
Staying quiet. Staying low. I'm a dock plant.
Mr. Gourd lifts a glowing pumpkin from the van. The coat swings open. Beneath it: one stylish black heel.
Mr. Gourd carries the pumpkin through a door marked SCIENCE BUILDING: LABORATORY ENTRANCE.
The pumpkins go to the lab. Whoever Mr. Gourd is, he's connected to the college.
On the dock rail, a crow watches Brad. It looks like it knows exactly who's under that mustache.

else.text: Brad slips away before Mr. Gourd returns. He has a stand to run, and a few new questions.

C_j.text: There you are! Dad says you chased a mustache across town.
I wore three raven hats. It's a long story.
McVine girl! A duel! Whoever sells the next pumpkin wins!
Mrs. Hollis returns, hopeful. Jane steps forward. Big Mel gets a sudden nervous twitch.
Rule one. Never say the price first. Rule two. Never smile first.
Rule three. Never lose to a man named Mel.
In under a minute, Mrs. Hollis pays forty dollars for a pumpkin and thanks Jane for the privilege.
That was the greatest thing I've ever seen.
Dad's counted every dollar since the tractor broke. Yet he sold forty Patch Seven pumpkins at full price.
That's not Dad. And if Patch Seven goes, we lose a third of our income.

C_j.prompt: Jane is worried about the farm.

options.text: Offer to help with a plan

do.text: Then we find another way. A haunted hayride. Cider. Pumpkin tours. Doris could have a fan club.
Doris would love a fan club.
...Thank you. For saying 'we'.
We could charge admission to see Doris. Five dollars. Two for children.
Ha! She'd work the crowd.
Jane laughs, but her eyes are still on the empty crates where the forty pumpkins were.

C_s.text: Beside the McVine stand, Sandra runs the Log & Stump's ale stall, glaring at anyone who comes close.
Sit. I have news. My regulars know everything.
A white van with a faculty permit, Lot C, leaves the college at dawn on Saturdays.
The janitor measured the footprints near the loading dock. Size seven. A heel.
Or a person in a man's mustache.
I'd like to know who. I'd like it very much.

C_s.prompt: Sandra stares at the college in the distance.

options.text: Set up a stakeout with her

do.text: Let's watch the dock tonight. Together.
A stakeout. With snacks. I'll bring the thermos.
Night. Behind the dumpster, Brad and Sandra whisper over a thermos of black coffee.
Movement. Trench coat. Gait: careful. Shoes: expensive.
A figure carries a pumpkin inside. A gust of wind lifts the collar, but the face stays in shadow.
I can't see a thing.
I can see a size seven. Now we know. Probably.
Sandra's elbow brushes Brad's. She doesn't move it.
You're the best detective in town. I trust you.
Flattery. It works, a little.
I'll find out. And I'll tell you first.

C_g.text: At the Grove Cafe stall, Georgia is test-driving her Halloween punch from a bubbling pumpkin bowl.
A line of shoppers forms. Each takes a cup. Each pauses mid-sip.

then.text: The punch glows faintly. A man blinks and says, 'I haven't called my mother in three weeks.'
Then he shrugs and walks off.
That's... milder than I thought. The dilution is working.

else.text: The punch glows bright. A woman says, 'I've used my neighbor's wifi for six years!'
A man weeps. Two strangers hug.
That's... a lot of honesty. For a test cup.

C_g.text: Brad. I think I'm making a very dangerous punch.

do.text: Let's fix it together. Less pumpkin. More cider. A lot more ginger.
They spend an hour tweaking quantities. The punch gets less glowy and more delicious.
This is the first time anyone's helped me bake instead of eating the mistakes.
Georgia. Don't serve it. It isn't safe.
But I promised. The committee's counting on me.
...You're right. I know you're right. It still hurts.

C_p.text: Mr. Gourd leaves the lab again, wiping his hands. A gust opens the coat and Brad sees the shoes.
Black. Pointed toe. Low heel. I've seen those shoes in the lecture hall.
A long pause. The man in the trench coat sighs and peels off the mustache.
Mr. Bart. This is... a theatrical production.
I am neutralizing them. Every one. Before the full moon. Halloween is eight days away.
My neutralizer treats forty a week. Patch Seven has hundreds. I cannot keep up.
Georgia is making two hundred cups of punch for the dance. From Patch Seven pumpkins.
...That is exactly what happened last time.
Gord shook your hand for a full minute. Does he know?
He always did. He plays along. We are not on speaking terms. We are on cooperating terms.

C_p.prompt: Patricia holds a mustache and a secret.

do.text: I'll help. I'll carry pumpkins. I'll do whatever you need.
You're the first person to offer. In twenty-five years.
Bring gloves. And do not mention the mustache to anyone.

options.text: Tell her you'll tell the others

do.text: People should know. Jane. Sandra. Georgia.
If everyone knows, there will be panic. That is how it went wrong the last time.
Please. I'm asking you. Not to.
I'll keep quiet. In exchange, you tell me everything. Before Halloween.
...A fair trade. I'll tell you what I can. In time.

C_p.text: Mr. Bart. The mustache goes back on. We were never here.

D_close.text: Dusk. The market empties. Gord counts the day's money at the stand.

then.text: A good day. Better than the last three combined. You've got a salesman's tongue, boy.

D_close.text: Uncle Gord. You sold forty Patch Seven pumpkins to a man in a mustache.
Everyone in Brad's life seems to be holding their breath.
Across town at the loading dock, the crow perches on the rail, watching the lab windows glow orange.
